title: Kedarkantha Trek
shortDescription: A classic Himalayan winter summit trek through snow-laden pine forests.
description: Kedarkantha is one of the most popular winter treks in India, famous for its stunning snow-covered trails, dense pine forests, and a summit climb that rewards you with 360-degree views of major Himalayan peaks like Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch, and Black Peak. The trail passes through charming campsites at Juda ka Talab and Kedarkantha Base, making it ideal for first-time Himalayan trekkers.

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.description: Drive from Dehradun to Sankri village (the base), a scenic 10-hour journey through the Govind National Park.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Juda ka Talab
itinerary.description: Trek through dense pine and maple forests to the frozen lake campsite of Juda ka Talab.

itinerary.title: Juda ka Talab to Kedarkantha Base
itinerary.description: Ascend through open meadows with widening views to reach the Kedarkantha Base camp.

itinerary.title: Summit Day and descent to Hargaon
itinerary.description: Early morning summit push to Kedarkantha peak for sunrise, then descend to Hargaon campsite.

itinerary.title: Hargaon to Sankri
itinerary.description: Descend back through the forest to Sankri village.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Dehradun
itinerary.description: Drive back to Dehradun, trek concludes.

title: Chembra Peak Trek
shortDescription: Wayanad's highest peak, home to the famous heart-shaped lake.
description: Chembra Peak is the highest peak in the Wayanad district of Kerala, set amid rolling tea estates and lush green hills. The trail is best known for its iconic heart-shaped lake, which is said to never dry up. The trek offers sweeping views of the Western Ghats and is a perfect short, rewarding day hike for nature lovers.

itinerary.title: Meppadi to Chembra Peak and back
itinerary.description: Obtain the forest pass at Meppadi, trek up through tea estates and grasslands to the heart-shaped lake and summit viewpoint, then descend the same route.

title: Hampta Pass Trek
shortDescription: A dramatic crossover trek from green Kullu valleys to the barren Spiti landscape.
description: Hampta Pass is a spectacular crossover trek that takes you from the lush green valleys of Kullu to the stark, desert-like terrain of Lahaul and Spiti in a single trail. Within a few days you walk through pine forests, grasslands, river crossings, and a high mountain pass at 4,270 m, ending with an optional visit to the surreal Chandratal Lake.

itinerary.title: Manali to Jobra, trek to Chika
itinerary.description: Short drive to Jobra, then an easy walk through forests to the Chika campsite beside the river.

itinerary.title: Chika to Balu ka Ghera
itinerary.description: Trek alongside the Rani river through meadows to the base camp of the pass.

itinerary.title: Balu ka Ghera to Shea Goru via Hampta Pass
itinerary.description: The big day: climb to Hampta Pass at 4,270 m for stunning views, then a steep descent to Shea Goru.

itinerary.title: Shea Goru to Chatru, drive to Chandratal
itinerary.description: Descend to Chatru and drive to the beautiful Chandratal Lake.

itinerary.title: Chatru to Manali
itinerary.description: Drive back to Manali over Rohtang Pass, trek concludes.

title: Triund Trek
shortDescription: A short, scenic weekend trek above McLeod Ganj with Dhauladhar views.
description: Triund is one of the most accessible Himalayan treks, perfect for beginners and weekend travellers. A steady climb from McLeod Ganj brings you to a grassy ridge offering panoramic views of the Dhauladhar range on one side and the Kangra valley on the other. Camping overnight under the stars at Triund is an unforgettable first taste of the mountains.
bestSeason: March to June, September to December

itinerary.title: McLeod Ganj to Triund
itinerary.description: Climb through oak and rhododendron forest to the Triund ridge, set up camp and enjoy sunset over the Dhauladhars.

itinerary.title: Triund to McLeod Ganj
itinerary.description: Catch sunrise over the snow peaks, then descend back to McLeod Ganj.

title: Valley of Flowers Trek
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage valley carpeted with hundreds of alpine flowers.
description: The Valley of Flowers is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Uttarakhand, renowned for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers that bloom in the monsoon months. The trek combines the vibrant valley with a visit to Hemkund Sahib, a high-altitude glacial lake and revered Sikh shrine. It is a paradise for nature lovers, botanists, and photographers.

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Govindghat
itinerary.description: Long scenic drive along the Alaknanda river to the road-head town of Govindghat.

itinerary.title: Govindghat to Ghangaria
itinerary.description: Trek (with optional pony/helicopter) up the valley to the base village of Ghangaria.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Valley of Flowers and back
itinerary.description: Day hike into the famous flower valley, returning to Ghangaria for the night.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Hemkund Sahib and back
itinerary.description: Steep climb to the glacial lake and gurudwara at Hemkund Sahib, then descend.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Govindghat
itinerary.description: Descend back to Govindghat.

itinerary.title: Govindghat to Rishikesh
itinerary.description: Drive back to Rishikesh, trek concludes.

title: Tadiandamol Trek
shortDescription: The highest peak in Coorg, through shola forests and rolling grasslands.
description: Tadiandamol is the highest peak in the Coorg (Kodagu) region of Karnataka. The trail winds through dense shola forests, open grasslands, and coffee country, offering misty Western Ghats views from the summit. It's a fairly short trek that can be done in a day, making it a favourite weekend escape from Bengaluru.

itinerary.title: Nalknad Palace to Tadiandamol summit and back
itinerary.description: Trek from the Nalknad Palace through shola forests and grassy ridges to the summit, then return by the same route.

title: Goechala Trek
shortDescription: An epic Sikkim trek to the foot of mighty Kanchenjunga.
description: Goechala is one of the most rewarding high-altitude treks in India, leading deep into the Kanchenjunga National Park in Sikkim. The trail rewards trekkers with up-close views of Mount Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, along with more than a dozen other summits, glacial lakes, and rhododendron forests. It is a demanding trek best suited to experienced hikers.
bestSeason: April to June, September to November

itinerary.title: Yuksom to Sachen
itinerary.description: Begin trekking from Yuksom through dense forest, crossing several bridges to reach Sachen.

itinerary.title: Sachen to Tshoka
itinerary.description: Cross the Prek Chu river and climb to the village of Tshoka.

itinerary.title: Tshoka to Dzongri
itinerary.description: Ascend through rhododendron forest to the alpine meadows of Dzongri.

itinerary.title: Dzongri acclimatisation and Dzongri Top
itinerary.description: Sunrise hike to Dzongri Top for panoramic Kanchenjunga views, rest and acclimatise.

itinerary.title: Dzongri to Thansing
itinerary.description: Descend to the Prek Chu valley and trek to Thansing.

itinerary.title: Thansing to Lamuney
itinerary.description: Short trek along the valley to Lamuney, the last campsite before the pass.

itinerary.title: Lamuney to Goechala viewpoint and back to Kokchurang
itinerary.description: Pre-dawn push to the Goechala viewpoint for sunrise on Kanchenjunga, then a long descent to Kokchurang.

itinerary.title: Kokchurang to Tshoka
itinerary.description: Trek back down through the forest to Tshoka.

itinerary.title: Tshoka to Yuksom
itinerary.description: Final descent back to Yuksom.

itinerary.title: Departure from Yuksom
itinerary.description: Drive out from Yuksom, trek concludes.

title: Sandakphu Trek
shortDescription: Walk the Singalila ridge to see four of the five highest peaks on Earth.
description: Sandakphu is the highest point in West Bengal, located on the Singalila ridge along the India-Nepal border. The trek is famous for offering views of four of the world's five highest peaks - Everest, Kanchenjunga, Lhotse, and Makalu - including the iconic 'Sleeping Buddha' formation. The trail passes through charming villages and the rhododendron-rich Singalila National Park.
bestSeason: October to December, March to May

itinerary.title: Maneybhanjang to Tumling
itinerary.description: Start from Maneybhanjang and trek along the ridge through Meghma to Tumling, crossing into Nepal-side trails.

itinerary.title: Tumling to Kalipokhri
itinerary.description: Walk through Singalila National Park forests to the sacred pond at Kalipokhri.

itinerary.title: Kalipokhri to Sandakphu
itinerary.description: Steep final climb to Sandakphu for sweeping views of the Sleeping Buddha and Everest range.

itinerary.title: Sandakphu to Sabargram
itinerary.description: Trek along the high ridge towards Phalut, camping at Sabargram.

itinerary.title: Sabargram to Gorkhey via Phalut
itinerary.description: Reach Phalut viewpoint, then descend steeply into the forested valley to Gorkhey.

itinerary.title: Gorkhey to Sepi, drive out
itinerary.description: Final short trek to Sepi and drive back to Darjeeling.
